newsitem.title: USA: Infinite Machines gets good PDT result.
newsitem.headline: Infinite Machines gets good PDT result.

text.p: Infinite Machines Corp said Wednesday that its Spectra Science Corp subsidiary has received positive results from a first round of invivo tests comparing the efficacy of Spectra's low-cost disposable light source with a costly, high-maintenance dye laser for use in photodynamic therapy (PDT) with Photofrin.
Infinite said results of skin sensitivity tests in a rat animal model showed that the two sources were completely equivalent.

"The determination of the equivalence between our disposable LaserPaint technology and a continuous wave dye laser for use with Photofrin is an important step toward validating and commercializing our technology," said Nabil Lawandy, chief executive officer of Spectra in a press release.
According to Infinite, Photofrin, made by QLT PhotoTherapeutics Inc,is the only FDA approved photodynamic therapy drug.
A spokesman for QLT was not immediately available to comment.
